composition.review_note: The previous wide native Mattermost sequence returns. Short attention boxes point at native owner replies, the approved finding, partial recovery, full delivery and retry. The original room/thread transitions and message arrivals remain visible.

opening_equivalence.note: Every decoded opening frame was compared after uniform downscaling. This verifies visual structure after re-encoding, not bit-identical compressed video.

method.note: ROI excludes toolbar clocks and composer. Only within-clip native source windows are compared. Candidate pixels not matching both original source frames are excluded, preventing annotation strokes from counting as UI motion. This confirms retained screen content changes; it is not a new model or service run.

motion_audit.note: Eight measurable message/approval changes across seven native windows match the actual earlier film. Within-clip content is tested, not camera cuts, zooms, clocks or newly drawn borders.

findings: The opening retains the important-message hook, clear company roles, privacy rationale and Here's how transition.
Maya's sharing reply is shown in the TeamChat workroom; the complete approved finding appears in the shared incident.
A finding and its evidence references are approved for disclosure; the narration does not claim that only the last question sentence crosses.
HarborCloud's reviewed result shows six successful connection checks while only fifteen of twenty-four app messages arrive.
Maya separately approves the app repair. The first twenty-four-of-twenty-four delivery check precedes the earlier-message retry.
The original failed message is recovered with unchanged identity/text, and the repeated request does not create another copy.
The final widened outlines surround the native text without cutting off author labels, line endings or approval descenders.

join_cues.text: Maya reports the problem in the shared incident channel and asks TeamChat's agent
to investigate. Leo, HarborCloud's engineer, replies that his team is available.

limits: This is an independent sampled visual, caption-timeline and source-matched screen-motion review, not a new live agent or service run.
The historical native source cadence is approximately five frames per second, rendered at twenty-four fps with the previous reading holds and edited waits retained.
The separate assembly manifest checks source PCM retention and decoding. This review does not claim a full independent auditory or streamed-YouTube playback review.
The companies and incident are fictional; one presenter roleplays both owners. No production isolation, automatic PII redaction or measured speed advantage is claimed.
